### LOW: Returned history reasoning is spliced into the GLM template without the native\-delimiter history check
[provider\-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Prompting/GLM5NextPromptPolicy\.swift:361](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/5c73e5e91f8db0193ebba960e62a058af19a9323/provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Prompting/GLM5NextPromptPolicy.swift#L361) · TB-007

\`RawControls\.capture\` now collects \`reasoning\` and \`reasoning\_details\[\]\.text\` from the raw \`messages\` array \(head 108\-112, 254\-275\)\. At head 361, that text is written into \`reasoning\_content\` for assistant turns that have none\. The SDK message type drops these fields, so \`validateHistory\(request\.messages\)\` at head 351 never sees them\. The protocol doc at protocol\-messages\.md:1152 says the policy rejects ambiguous native delimiters in history, but this injected text appears to bypass that check\. A caller could put GLM control tokens in a history \`reasoning\` string, such as \`</think>\`, \`<tool\_call>\`/\`<arg\_value>\` or role markers\. The result would be renderer\-confusing prompt structure that the provider treats as validated history\. The impact visible here is limited to the caller's own request: prompt structure/contract integrity, tool\-call parsing confusion, and a possible \`prompt\_work\` exact\-count divergence from the platform sidecar\. No cross\-tenant disclosure is shown\. Fix: apply the same native\-delimiter rejection to captured returned reasoning before injection\. Alternatively, route it through \`validateHistory\` and add a regression test\.
